title: AisleLens Standard Grammar — 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2
description: The grammar for an AisleLens category standard: a published, versioned, executable set of assertions about what a product page claims, with defined evidence rules. Validated by standards/validate.ts, which implements the subset of JSON Schema used here. Governance rules that a schema cannot express (the never-weaken rule's window semantics, hash canonicalisation) are enforced by standards/__tests__ and stated in SCHEMA.md.

grammar_version.description:
The version of THIS grammar the standard is authored against. A standard is only readable against a stated grammar version, and A VERSION IS NEVER REDEFINED once a document has been published against it — a grammar version resolves through the same citation contract as a standard hash.

1.0 assigns the `not_discriminating` tier from an AUTHORED PREDICTION, and requires `predicted_discrimination` (a numeric band) on every entry.

1.1 (2026-07-27) adds the `applied_by_author` status, per-entry `measured_discrimination` in its FIRST shape (`fail_rate_pct`/`asked`/`verdict`/`carries_information`/`source`), per-entry `supersedes`, and the top-level `measured_fitness` block — every addition OPTIONAL, so a grammar-1.0 document validates unchanged against this schema and its content hash is untouched. `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` is authored against it and is byte-frozen.

1.2 IS THE RECONCILIATION OF TWO GRAMMARS THAT WERE BOTH AUTHORED AS 1.1, and it exists as 1.2 rather than as a redefinition of 1.1 because a published, hash-frozen document already declares 1.1: redefining that name would make a citable document invalid against the version it names. What 1.2 changes, and why: THE BAND WAS MEASURED WRONG. Authored fail-rate bands HELD 1 OF 10 on the 100-product coffee sample (2 of 10 on the earlier 43-product one), and EVERY MISS WAS HIGH — the author systematically over-estimated how much a category's stores publish. A field wrong nine times in ten in a known direction is worse than no field, because it looks like information. So at 1.2: `predicted_discrimination` is FORBIDDEN and `discrimination_prediction` (a direction and a confidence, NO number) is optional in its place; a discrimination verdict is a MEASUREMENT with an interval, a minimum n and a recorded sample (`$defs/discriminationMeasurement`); `not_discriminating` is reachable ONLY through such a measurement; `category_fitness` replaces `measured_fitness` and gates publication; and the new tier `unbound` names the state a question is in when the engine could run it and this standard has not authored a binding. 1.0 and 1.1 documents remain valid and readable against the rules they were authored under. See SCHEMA.md §9.

standard_id.description: Stable family identifier, e.g. ALS-COFFEE. Never reused for a different category.

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR. A MAJOR bump means a conformance result under the old version is not comparable to one under the new.

status.description: draft = authored, never applied to a real store by anyone. applied_by_author = the authoring party has executed it against a real sample and published the measurement, but NO SECOND PARTY has applied it; a document in this state may be cited and must not be described as settled. published = released for third-party application; PROMOTION TO IT REQUIRES a second party to have run the document without the authoring party's involvement, which is the same bar as posture.independently_applied and must be recorded in the changelog — and at grammar 1.2 it additionally requires a `category_fitness` record, because a standard whose error rate on its OWN category has never been measured cannot tell a merchant what a failure of it means. withdrawn = must no longer be cited. `applied_by_author` exists because v1.0 spent a day in a state where `draft` was false (it had been executed against 100 real products and published at a stable URL) and `published` would have been a lie (nobody else had touched it). A document that is wrong about itself is the failure mode this project treats as unrecoverable, and it does not become acceptable because the error is modest.

independently_applied.description: TRUE only once a second party has applied this standard without the authoring party's involvement. While FALSE, this document is a rubric with a versioned changelog, not a standard, and the statement below must say so in the published artifact.

category_signals.description: Which product fields decide whether this standard applies. Mirrors the engine's own inference order, which is deliberate: a standard that classifies products differently from the engine that runs it will fire on the wrong products.

out_of_scope.description: An explicit statement of what the standard does NOT attempt to adjudicate. Required and non-empty: a standard that does not bound itself will be read as bounding nothing.

requirement_kinds_used.description: Every engine requirement kind this standard binds to. Must be a subset of the kinds the engine exports.

standard_hash.description: A content hash so a citation resolves to a specific text. Computed over the canonical form of the standard with this object removed — see SCHEMA.md and standards/hash.ts.

category_fitness.description: GRAMMAR 1.2. THE PUBLICATION GATE: required when status is `published`, and forbidden at 1.0/1.1, where the property does not exist. It is the migrated `measured_fitness` — a rename, not an alias, so no document carries both names for the same quantity. See $defs/categoryFitness.

measured_fitness.description: GRAMMAR 1.0 AND 1.1 ONLY — `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` carries one, so it cannot be removed from the grammar. Forbidden at 1.2, where `category_fitness` replaces it.

withdrawn_entries.description: Entry ids from the PREVIOUS version that this one does not carry, each with a reason. A question that quietly disappears between versions is a coverage change nobody can see; every prior id must either be superseded by an entry here or appear in this list.

allOf.description:
CP3 — A STANDARD MAY NOT PUBLISH WITHOUT A FITNESS MEASUREMENT ON ITS OWN CATEGORY. Every figure here is from `standards/coffee/v1.0/fitness.json`; none is restated from memory. Same engine, same audit discipline: the COFFEE sample (77 storefronts, 100 products, 162 pass rows each audited individually against full untruncated evidence) confirmed 10 false positives — 12.78% cluster-adjusted at ICC 0.2. The GENERAL DTC sample (172 products over 169 stores, 509 pass rows) confirmed 18 — 7.80%, AND THAT ONE IS A FLOOR: only a single defect class has been re-checked mechanically, so the two samples are not audited to the same depth and their ratio is not itself a measurement. The coffee defects fire on copy only a coffee page writes — a brewing recipe or a caffeine dose read as the bag's own weight, the soil-science sense of `organic`, `single-origin` inside a sentence describing a blend. A general-sample bound estimates the error rate on copy that looks like the average of every category at once, which is copy no merchant writes. The number that matters to a coffee roaster is 12.78%.

⚠️ THIS GATE IS GRAMMAR 1.2 AND IS NOT RETRO-FITTED. 1.0 and 1.1 shipped with no publication gate at all, and applying one to them now would change what an already-published version means — the same reason the reconciled grammar is 1.2 rather than a redefinition of 1.1. Nothing escapes through the gap: no 1.0 or 1.1 document in this repo is `published` (coffee v1.0 is `draft`, coffee v1.1 is `applied_by_author`, the accessory draft is `draft`), and `applied_by_author` exists precisely so that a document which has been measured but not independently applied does not have to overstate itself to describe itself.

completion_state.description: INCOMPLETE blocks publication. A measurement that did not complete is not a passing measurement.

allOf.description:
GRAMMAR 1.0 AND 1.1 — ONE RULE, BECAUSE ON THIS AXIS THE TWO VERSIONS ARE IDENTICAL. The numeric prediction band is REQUIRED on every entry, the reshaped 1.2 prediction may not appear, `measured_discrimination` is the FIRST shape, the tier vocabulary is the original four, and `category_fitness` does not exist yet.

⚠️ THESE ARE NOT THE RULES A CORRECTED GRAMMAR WOULD CHOOSE, AND THEY ARE FROZEN ANYWAY. `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` carries `predicted_discrimination` on all 42 entries and five `not_discriminating` tiers with no measurement behind any of them — the exact defect grammar 1.2 exists to close. It stays valid here because it is published and hash-frozen, and a document must remain readable against the rules it was authored under. Fixing it is a REISSUE at 1.2, not an edit: see SCHEMA.md §9.3.

tier.description: `unbound` is a 1.2 tier. A 1.0 or 1.1 reader has no definition for it, and a tier a reader cannot resolve is worse than the wrong tier.

allOf.description: GRAMMAR 1.2 ENTRY RULES. The band is REMOVED, not deprecated in place; a measurement is a `$defs/discriminationMeasurement` with an interval, a derived minimum n and a recorded sample; and `measured_fitness` is gone in favour of `category_fitness` — a MIGRATION, not an alias, so a 1.2 document cannot carry both names for the same quantity and leave a reader to pick.

CP1 — `not_discriminating` IS A MEASURED VERDICT AND CANNOT BE REACHED FROM A PREDICTION. Under 1.0 an author wrote `in_target_band: false` and the entry became `not_discriminating`: published, and never run. WEIGHT-001 was flagged that way from a band of 15-40% against 1 of 9 products, and measured 49.0% over 100 — the most informative split in the standard, one reclassification away from deletion. The schema now rejects the tier without a measurement that says so.

reqKind.description: The engine's complete ReqKind union (src/server/productTest.ts). There is no ninth kind.

evidenceSurface.description: The engine's nine QuotableSurface values, plus the three non-text structural surfaces it also reads (variant price, variant availability, JSON-LD identifier), plus external_register which the engine cannot read at all and which therefore forces tier=blocked.

nonPublicSurface.description: Surfaces a free public test cannot reach. Named here so the constraint is data rather than prose.

operator.description: Closed operator vocabulary. A new operator is a grammar change (MAJOR), not an authoring choice. `includes_buyer_parameter` was ADDED in the course of authoring the device-accessory draft: every other operator compares page evidence against a value authored into the standard, while a compatibility assertion compares a merchant-published LIST against a value the BUYER supplies at test time. Entries using it must carry `buyer_parameter`.

assertion.description: The machine form of the question: attribute, operator, expected value.

subject.description: The product property under assertion, in snake_case. Not an engine key — the engine binding lives in `binding`.

expected.description: The expected value. `true` for presence operators; a string or array for value operators; an object for derived ones.

unit.description: Where the expected value carries a unit.

registry.description: Where the claim could resolve against an external register. Present on every entry; `resolvable: false` is a finding, not an omission.

lookup_key.description: The key a lookup needs. If a product page does not carry this key, the register cannot verify the page's claim however public it is.

resolves_to_level.description: The level the register resolves to. A company-level record cannot verify a specific bag's claim, and conflating the two is the most likely way a registry assertion overclaims.

engine_can_perform.description: Whether the AisleLens engine can perform this lookup today. Always false in grammar v1.0 — there is no register client. A true value here without an engine change is a false statement.

grounding.description: Why this question is in the standard. MANDATORY. No question enters because it sounds plausible.

demand_basis.description: `trade_convention_only` is a WARNING label: it marks a question the trade cares about and shoppers may not, and it must never be the sole basis for an executable entry.

refutation.description: What the independent refuting pass said. Recorded in the published artifact so a reader can see the grounding was attacked, not just asserted.

binding.description: The engine Requirement this entry compiles to. Required for tier=executable and forbidden otherwise — an unbound `executable` claim is unverifiable, and a bound `advisory` one is a lie about what gets run.

claim.description: Engine CLAIM_TERMS key. Required when req_kind=claim.

attribute.description: Engine ATTRIBUTE_SPECS key. Required when req_kind=attribute.

label.description: The string the engine renders. LINTED by src/server/claimLinter.ts, and a violation returns the merchant's ENTIRE report as unreachable. See SCHEMA.md §6.

passing_states.description: Which engine states count as conformant FOR THIS ENTRY. `pass_no_blocking` is an absence-based inference and is only correct for req_kind=no_subscription; listing it anywhere else claims proof the engine did not produce.

predictedDiscrimination.description:
GRAMMAR 1.0 AND 1.1 ONLY, REQUIRED THERE, AND MEASURED WRONG. A HYPOTHESIS about how well the assertion discriminates, never a fact. Target band 15-85%: a requirement that fails for everyone and one that fails for no one carry the same information, which is none.

⚠️ THE MEASURED CALIBRATION OF THIS FIELD, AND IT GOT WORSE WITH MORE DATA. On the first valid sample — 43 coffee brands, applicability enforced, brands deduplicated — the ten authored bands HELD 2 OF 10 with all eight misses HIGH. On 100 products they HELD 1 OF 10 (`standards/coffee/v1.0/fitness.json`, `entry_discrimination.bands_held`), the survivor being GRIND-001 at 84.8% against 55-85%. The author systematically over-estimated how much a category's stores publish, and there is no evidence a different author in a different category would not. A field wrong nine times in ten in a known direction is worse than no field, because it looks like information. Grammar 1.2 replaces it with `discrimination_prediction`, which carries a direction and a confidence and no number.

⚠️ THREE NUMBERS THAT ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER, and they have been run together before. `bands held 1 of 10` = the prediction was right once. `above its band 8 of 10` = the entry discriminates LESS than predicted. `carries information 4 of 10` = the MEASURED rate lands inside 15-85%. FORMAT-001 at 73.7% against a predicted 30-60% is above its band and squarely inside the informative one; `above its band` does not mean `carries no information`.

⚠️ NEVER OVERWRITE A PREDICTION WITH ITS MEASUREMENT. The calibration above is computable only because the predictions were preserved beside the measured rates. A measured rate goes in `measured_discrimination`; this block keeps saying what was predicted.

in_target_band.description: ⚠️ THE FIELD THAT DROVE TIER ASSIGNMENT, AND THE REASON GRAMMAR 1.2 EXISTS. A false value here made an entry `not_discriminating` — published and never run — on the strength of a guess. WEIGHT-001 was predicted 15-40%, measured 11.1% at n=9, flagged accordingly, and then measured 48.8% at n=43 and 49.0% at n=100: the most stable figure in the document and its most informative split. Removed in grammar 1.2.

measured.description: FALSE while the band is a hypothesis. TRUE requires a recorded measurement, a changelog entry, and a sibling `measured_discrimination` block on the same entry — enforced by the entry-level `allOf`. It was `const: false` under grammar 1.0, when no AisleLens standard had ever been run against real stores; loosening it to a boolean is what grammar 1.1 did, and `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` carries `measured: true` on ten entries, so it CANNOT be tightened back to a const without invalidating a hash-frozen published document. THE BAND ITSELF IS NEVER REWRITTEN — a measured rate goes in `measured_discrimination`, and this block keeps saying what was predicted. That is not bookkeeping: the calibration that condemned the band (held 1 of 10, every miss high) is computable ONLY because the predictions were preserved beside the measured rates. A field nobody records cannot be shown to be wrong.

measuredDiscrimination.description:
GRAMMAR 1.0 AND 1.1 ONLY — the FIRST shape of a measurement, and the one `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` actually contains on ten entries. Kept verbatim, and kept valid, because that document is byte-frozen and every citation against it resolves through its hash. The MEASURED counterpart to predicted_discrimination, published BESIDE it and never in place of it. Present only on entries actually run against a recorded sample.

⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT DO, WHICH IS WHY 1.2 REPLACED IT WITH `$defs/discriminationMeasurement`. It records a point estimate and a denominator and nothing else: no interval, so a verdict cannot be checked against the arithmetic that would support it; no minimum n, so a rate over nine rows and a rate over a hundred read identically; no sample provenance, so a sample of t-shirts and a sample of coffee are indistinguishable; and a two-valued `verdict` measured against a PREDICTED band rather than a target one. `carries_information` is a point estimate compared to 15-85%, which is how GRIND-001 (84.8%, interval [76.5, 90.6]) reads as informative when its interval crosses the edge and decides nothing.

fail_rate_pct.description: Over the products the entry was ASKED, never over the sample size. A product the applicability predicate excluded contributes nothing, and dividing by the full sample would convert 'not asked' into 'failed'.

verdict.description: above_band = the real fail rate is HIGHER than predicted, so the entry discriminates LESS: nearly every store fails it, and a row everybody fails separates nobody from anybody.

carries_information.description: Whether the MEASURED rate sits inside the 15-85% target band. This is the DISCRIMINATION question and it is separate from the CONFORMANCE question: an entry almost every store fails is useless as a discriminator and entirely legitimate as a requirement. Nothing is ever deleted for failing this.

source.description: The record the number came from, so a reader can go and check it.

measuredFitness.description:
GRAMMAR 1.0 AND 1.1 ONLY, and RENAMED (not aliased) to `category_fitness` at 1.2. THE ERROR RATE OF THE ENGINE WHILE EXECUTING THIS STANDARD, measured BEFORE this version was published and therefore carried inside the document. A measurement taken AFTER publication must go in the fitness.json sidecar instead, because standard_hash covers these bytes and a citation resolves through it — which is exactly why v1.0's measurement is a sidecar and this one is not.

⚠️ THE 1.2 NAME IS `category_fitness`, AND THE RENAME IS THE POINT. `measured_fitness` says only that the number was measured, which at 1.2 every number in a document is. `category_fitness` says the thing that decides whether the document may publish: fitness ON THIS CATEGORY. The same engine measured 7.80% over a general DTC sample and 12.78% over a coffee one (`standards/coffee/v1.0/fitness.json`), so a fitness figure with no category attached is not a weaker version of this field — it is a different quantity. `$defs/categoryFitness` additionally requires the sample provenance, the audit discipline, all three bounds, a completion state and stated limits, none of which this shape can express.

is_floor.description: Only PART of this sample has been re-checked, so its rate is a LOWER BOUND. A floor and a complete audit must never be compared as peers.

addressed_by_a_guard.description: FALSE means no mechanism in the engine addresses this class at all. Publishing that is the point.

discriminationPrediction.description:
GRAMMAR 1.2. The reshaped prediction: a DIRECTION and a CONFIDENCE, which is all an author who has not measured can honestly supply, plus the reasoning, which is the only part of the old field that ever carried value.

⚠️ THE BIAS AN AUTHOR MUST READ BEFORE FILLING THIS IN. Bands authored without measurement have held 2 of 10 on the 43-product sample and 1 OF 10 on the 100-product one, WITH EVERY MISS HIGH — the author expected stores to publish more than they do, and measuring more of them made the record worse, not better. Scored on the ten entries of the 43-product run, a three-valued direction would have been right 5 of 10 (95% CI 24-76%, which at ten entries is not distinguishable from a coin); that scoring has NOT been redone on the 100-product run, so treat it as the best available figure and not as a current one. So this field is OPTIONAL and it is UNRANKED: it may not determine `tier`, it may not determine a `measured_discrimination.verdict`, and no test may read it. It exists to record the author's reasoning so a later measurement can falsify it, and for no other purpose.

Deliberately carries NO number. A band authored wide enough to always hold carries no information, which is the failure it was supposed to detect.

⚠️ KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, AND THE REASON IS THE INSTRUMENT. A field that by construction determines nothing looks like pure authoring cost. It survives because `bands held 1 of 10, every miss high` is computable ONLY because the predictions were preserved beside the measured rates — deleting the field destroys the instrument that produced the most useful sentence this programme has written about its own authoring. The cost objection is answered by `no_prediction` being first-class: an author with no grounded expectation writes one word.

direction.description: `no_prediction` is a first-class and often correct value. An author with no grounded expectation should say so rather than manufacture one.

confidence.description: `high` requires the reasoning to cite something measured, not something assumed.

sampleProvenance.description: How a sample was drawn. Every field here exists because its absence produced a wrong number in a real run.

category_scope.description:
THE CP3 GATE. `general_mixed_category` may never back a published error bound: the same engine measured 7.80% over 509 general-sample pass rows and 12.78% over 162 coffee pass rows (`standards/coffee/v1.0/fitness.json`), because category vocabulary produces category-specific false passes a broad sample structurally cannot contain.

⚠️ AND THE GENERAL FIGURE IS A FLOOR, WHICH SHARPENS THE RULE RATHER THAN SOFTENING IT. It was published as 0.83% over 507 rows with ZERO confirmed false positives, from an audit that read every rendered row. One mechanical check of one class — `identifiers` rows passing on an `mpn` that is the store's own Shopify product id — found eighteen in that same sample, because that row RENDERS NO QUOTE and is therefore invisible to any audit that reads rendered evidence, however many rows it reads. The two samples are not audited to the same depth, so the ratio between them is not a measurement; the DIRECTION is what this gate rests on.

category_standard_id.description: Required when category_scope is `this_category`, and the test suite additionally asserts it equals the document's own standard_id — a cross-field check JSON Schema cannot express.

selection.description: ⚠️ `first_handle` IS A KNOWN-DEFECTIVE SELECTION and the publication gate rejects it. Roasters lead their catalogue with merchandise: taking each store's first product handle captured t-shirts, mugs, a tote bag and a cocktail shaker, and 16 of 25 of the first run's products should never have been asked at all.

deduplicated_by_brand.description: ⚠️ MUST BE TRUE TO PUBLISH. `deathwishcoffee.com` and `www.deathwishcoffee.com` are one brand; they produced the same product and therefore the same false positive twice, and inflated the denominator. Inflating a denominator flatters a bound.

applicability_gate_enforced.description: ⚠️ MUST BE TRUE TO PUBLISH. Applicability is a precondition, not a field. Run against run 1's own snapshots the shipped predicate excluded 16 of 25 products; a standard applied uniformly is the cruelty_free failure with a version number on it.

unclassifiable_refused.description: Products the applicability predicate could not classify and therefore REFUSED. `unknown` is not the same as out-of-category and must not be silently treated as in-category: the shipped predicate is stricter than the hand count that preceded it precisely because it refuses what it cannot classify.

attrition_logged.description: Whether every attempted target that produced no product was logged with a cause. A sample whose attrition is unlogged cannot be shown to be unbiased.

discriminationMeasurement.description:
CP1 — A DISCRIMINATION VERDICT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN AUTHORING GUESS. An entry that compiles and executes is `executable` and stays executable until a record of this shape says otherwise.

MINIMUM n IS ENFORCED HERE AND IT IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. Below 22 adjudicated rows no observation whatsoever — not even 0/n or n/n, the two most extreme results obtainable — can place a 95% Wilson interval entirely outside the 15-85% target band. Formally n > z²(1-b)/b with z=1.96 and b=0.15 gives 21.77, so 22. A verdict recorded below that is arithmetically incapable of supporting the conclusion it states, which is why the floor is a schema `minimum` and not a guideline. Derivation and worked table: SCHEMA.md §9.2.

MINIMUM n IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and the evidence for that is documentary rather than statistical. WEIGHT-001 measured 1 of 9 (Wilson 2.0-43.5%) and then 21 of 43 (48.8%, Wilson 34.6-63.2%). The later POINT ESTIMATE falls outside the earlier interval — but the two intervals OVERLAP, and Fisher's exact test on the pair gives p=0.062, so the disagreement is NOT established as beyond sampling error and nothing here claims it is. What IS established is separate and stronger: re-running the applicability predicate over run 1's own snapshots excluded 16 of its 25 products as merchandise, so run 1's sample was invalid on its own terms. A verdict can be defeated by a bad sample at any n, which is what `sample` exists to record.

verdict.description:
THE RULE IS ASYMMETRIC ON PURPOSE, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT. `standards/discrimination.ts#verdictFor` is the authority; this text describes it and may not drift from it.

`not_discriminating` = THE WHOLE 95% INTERVAL lies outside the target band. Only then may an entry be retired.
`discriminating` = THE POINT ESTIMATE lies inside the band. That is all KEEPING an entry requires.
`indeterminate` = the rate is outside the band but the interval is not wholly outside: the measurement RAN, is recorded, and decides nothing. The entry stays executable and keeps running.

Hard to leave, easy to return. Retirement is a one-way door — an entry that is not run cannot produce the evidence that would reverse the decision to stop running it — so it demands the whole interval. Keeping a row costs a noisy line in a report, so it demands only the rate. A symmetric rule requiring the whole interval INSIDE the band to keep an entry would retire nothing and demote almost everything to `indeterminate`, which is why it is not the rule.

Three states rather than two, for the same reason src/measure/completion.ts has three: a measurement that could not decide must never read as one that decided.

WHAT THE THIRD STATE IS WORTH, MEASURED. Re-deriving the ten coffee entries from experiments/v3-2/standard_run3.jsonl gives discriminating 4 / indeterminate 1 / not_discriminating 5. The shipped 1.1 document, which had only two states, reports carries_information true for the same four. The single disagreement is where the third state earns its place: SOURCE-001 at 89.0% reads as a clean `false` — a settled no-information verdict — and its interval [81.4, 93.7] crosses 85, so the measurement in fact decides nothing. A two-valued verdict has to call that, and calls it wrongly.

n_asked.description: Rows the entry was asked of, including those the engine could not adjudicate. REQUIRED, because the gap between asked and adjudicated is the record's only visible handle on missingness and it is not ignorable: DELIV-001's 11 unadjudicated rows are 25.6% of what it was asked, and the three readings of that entry (drop them, count them as fails, count them as passes) give 59.4%, 69.8% and 44.2%. Publishing only the adjudicated count hides which reading was taken.

n_adjudicated.description: Rows the engine actually decided. THE RATE AND THE INTERVAL ARE COMPUTED OVER THIS, NEVER OVER n_asked: `requires_store_access` is not a fail, and counting it as one silently changes the answer — DELIV-001 is 59.4% over 32 adjudicated rows and 44.2% over 43 asked.

interval_95.description: Wilson score interval, recomputed and checked against fail_count/n_adjudicated by the test suite — a published interval nobody recomputes is a number, not evidence.

target_band.description:
The band the interval is compared against. PINNED to the grammar's 15-85%, and stated in the record so a reader can recompute the floor rather than trust it.

⚠️ IT IS A `const` AND NOT A FREE NUMBER FOR A MEASURED REASON. `n_adjudicated.minimum` is hard-coded to 22, which is the floor DERIVED FROM THIS BAND: n > z²(1-b)/b. The floor moves steeply with the edge — 73 at 5%, 35 at 10%, 22 at 15%, 16 at 20%, 12 at 25% — so a record free to declare a 10-90% band would pass the schema at n=22 while its own derived floor was 35. That is precisely the 'quietly weakened the rule' failure this floor exists to prevent, reintroduced by the field meant to make it auditable. Changing the band is a GRAMMAR change, and it recomputes the minimum.

decision_rule.description: The only rule this grammar defines. Naming it in the record means a later change of rule is visible rather than silent.

instrument_bias.description:
R3 — THE INSTRUMENT GATE. A confidence interval bounds SAMPLING error and nothing else; it does not cover a known one-directional bias in the engine doing the measuring. Required (possibly empty, which is itself a claim) whenever the verdict is `not_discriminating`, because that is the only verdict that deletes something.

The measurement that forced it: the one entry run 2's arithmetic permits retiring, CERT-002, clears the band edge by 2.94pp — and it is a CLAIM row, measured with the semantic tier off, which can only overstate a claim row's fail rate. One row reclassified from fail to pass takes it to 41 of 43 and refuses. On an instrument whose false-pass rate on this category's copy is 6.17% point / 12.78% cluster-adjusted 95% bound (`standards/coffee/v1.0/fitness.json`), a retirement decided by a 2.94pp margin is decided by the instrument rather than by the stores. Under R3, run 2 licenses ZERO retirements.

direction.description: Which way the bias moves the measured rate. Only a bias pushing TOWARD the band edge the interval cleared can have manufactured the retirement.

magnitude_pp.description: Omit when the bias is real but unquantified. An unquantified bias toward the cleared edge BLOCKS retirement outright: it cannot be shown to be smaller than the margin.

supersedes.description: CP1 — WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A RE-MEASUREMENT CONTRADICTS AN EARLIER ONE. Append-only: a superseded measurement is never deleted, because the disagreement is itself the finding. Three of run 1's ten verdicts were artefacts of n=9 and deleting them would have erased the evidence that small samples invert verdicts.

priorMeasurement.description: A measurement this record replaces, kept in the document.

superseded_because.description: ⚠️ `larger_sample` IS NOT AN EXPLANATION FOR DISJOINT INTERVALS. Size alone widens or narrows an interval; it does not move it off the old one. When two measurements' 95% intervals do not overlap, something systematic differs and it must be named — the test suite rejects `larger_sample` in that case. This is exactly the WEIGHT-001 history: 11.1% at n=9 and 48.8% at n=43 do not overlap, and the reason is not that 43 is bigger than 9, it is that run 1's sample was t-shirts and mugs.

categoryFitness.description: CP3 — THE FITNESS OF THE ENGINE ON THIS CATEGORY'S COPY, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT NUMBER FROM ITS FITNESS IN GENERAL. Required to publish. See the root `allOf` for the evidence.

pass_rows_audited.description: Rows that PASSED and were then read individually. Fail rows carry no false-positive information.

row_by_row.description: Every pass row read, not a sample of them. Two prior audits of 37 and 18 rows reported zero false positives; an audit of 100 rows then found two.

untruncated_evidence.description: ⚠️ MUST BE TRUE. Auditors read the full evidence sentence, not the 180-character rendered quote. Two separate audits nearly mis-classified a real row because the supporting text sat past the cut.

borderline_recorded.description: Judgement calls counted as passes are NAMED so the call can be disputed. An audit whose judgement calls are invisible cannot be checked.

bounds.description: ALL THREE BOUNDS, NEVER ONE. Publishing the naive bound alone understates: rows are clustered within stores, and the cluster-adjusted number is the honest headline (10.47% naive versus 12.78% adjusted on the coffee sample, at 2.1 rows per store and a design effect of 1.22). Publishing only the per-store rate hides row-level exposure.

completion_state.description: src/measure/completion.ts applied to the fitness run. `INCOMPLETE` blocks publication rather than reading as clean: a measurement that did not complete is not a passing measurement, and zero is the most dangerous number a broken instrument returns because it is also what a healthy one returns.

defects.description: The confirmed false positives, each reproducible. A bound with no named defects behind it cannot be checked or fixed.

category_specific.description: Whether the defect fires on vocabulary this category's pages carry and a general sample does not. Most of coffee's ten do — a brewing recipe, a caffeine dose per serving, soil rich in organic matter, `single-origin` inside a sentence describing a blend — and that is the whole mechanism behind the gap between the two bounds.

limits.description: What this measurement did NOT establish, stated by the party publishing it. Never empty: a fitness record with no limits is a claim of completeness no sample of this size supports.

adversarial.description: The result of attacking THIS entry: store copy that satisfies the letter and violates the spirit. Required for tier=executable. An assertion that has not been attacked is an assertion that has not been tested.

attack.description: Verbatim copy that would pass the assertion while misleading a buyer.

residual_risk.description: What the attack can still achieve after the fix. Honest residual risk beats a claim of immunity.

id.description: Stable, citable, versioned: ALS-{CATEGORY}-{VERSION}-{CLASS}-{NNN}. An agency must be able to write 'your PDPs fail ALS-COFFEE-1.0-DECAF-002' in a client report and have it resolve.

question.description: Plain language, as a shopper would ask it. This is the consumer-facing half of the document and it is not optional for blocked or advisory entries.

buyer_parameter.description: A value the BUYER supplies at test time rather than one authored into the standard. Required when the operator is `includes_buyer_parameter` and forbidden otherwise. This field exists because the grammar's original assumption — that an assertion's expected value is fixed when the standard is written — is false for any compatibility claim, where the question is whether the buyer's own model appears in the seller's list.

tier.description:
WHY THE ENTRY IS OR IS NOT RUN. Each value states a DIFFERENT fact, and the whole point of having five is that a document may not park a question under a label that is false about it.

• `executable` = the engine runs it today. Requires a binding, an adversarial pass and a pass_means.

• `advisory` = A REAL BUYER QUESTION THAT PUBLIC DATA CANNOT ADJUDICATE. The obstacle is the EVIDENCE: no public surface carries it. Published, never tested.

• `blocked` = it should be executable and THE ENGINE CANNOT YET. The obstacle is the CODE, and it is named: `blocked_by` must cite a `G-NN` identifier in ENGINE_GAPS.md.

• `unbound` = ADDED AT GRAMMAR 1.2. The engine CAN run this kind and public data CAN adjudicate it — and THIS STANDARD has not authored the binding or put it through the adversarial pass. The obstacle is neither the evidence nor the engine: it is unwritten work in this document, and `unbound_reason` must name the engine `ReqKind` that fits. It exists because correcting the `not_discriminating` rule left five real entries with nowhere honest to go: filing them `advisory` would state that public data cannot adjudicate a published price or a stock flag, and filing them `blocked` would state that an engine kind that demonstrably exists does not. Both are false sentences in a published document, which is the failure this project treats as unrecoverable, so the grammar gained the missing name instead. `unbound` adds no matcher, no category and no executable entry — it is a state the document is already in, said out loud.

• `not_discriminating` = the engine COULD run it and deliberately does not, because it was MEASURED and the whole 95% interval lies outside the 15-85% target band, so the row separates nobody from anybody. AT GRAMMAR 1.2 THIS IS A MEASURED VERDICT, NOT AN AUTHORING CHOICE: it requires a `measured_discrimination` whose verdict is `not_discriminating`, and the schema rejects the tier without one. Under 1.0/1.1 it was assigned from a predicted band, which is exactly the field that held 1 of 10; WEIGHT-001 was flagged that way at n=9 and measured 49.0% at n=100. Published either way so a reader can see the question was considered.

applicability.description: When the entry applies. A decaf-method assertion must not fire on caffeinated coffee — an entry asked of the wrong product is the cruelty-free failure with a version number on it.

signal.description: How applicability is decided from readable data. `undecidable_from_public_data` is an honest value and forces the entry out of tier=executable unless the engine gates it.

insufficient_evidence.description: What explicitly does NOT count. THE DIFFERENTIATOR FIELD. This is where the standard states that 'chemical-free' does not establish Swiss Water process. Never empty — the schema forbids it and the test suite re-checks it.

conflict_rules.description: What to do when two surfaces disagree. At minimum one rule, because two surfaces disagreeing is the normal case, not the exception.

public_inspectable.description: Whether a free public test can adjudicate it. TRUE requires that no accepted_evidence surface is in nonPublicSurface — enforced by the test suite, not by the schema.

evidence_surfaces.description: Denormalised surface list, so surface constraints are checkable without walking accepted_evidence. Must equal the set of surfaces in accepted_evidence.

predicted_discrimination.description: Grammar 1.0 and 1.1 only, and REQUIRED at both — the root `allOf` makes it mandatory there and forbidden at 1.2.

discrimination_prediction.description: Grammar 1.2 only, and OPTIONAL there. Forbidden at 1.0 and 1.1. The two prediction shapes never coexist in one document: a reader who has to work out which one a given entry meant is reading two grammars at once.

measured_discrimination.description:
ONE FIELD NAME, TWO SHAPES, RESOLVED BY THE DOCUMENT'S OWN `grammar_version` — never by guessing from the keys present. At 1.0 and 1.1 it is `$defs/measuredDiscrimination`, the shape `ALS-COFFEE 1.1` actually contains; at 1.2 it is `$defs/discriminationMeasurement`, which adds the interval, the derived minimum n, the three-valued verdict and the sample provenance. The narrowing is done by the top-level `allOf`; the `anyOf` here is the floor, so the field can never be left wholly unchecked if a future version is added to the enum and its gate is forgotten.

OPTIONAL AT EVERY VERSION. Absent means UNMEASURED, which is not the same as measured-and-fine — and at 1.2 unmeasured is a perfectly legitimate state for an executable entry, which is why an entry stays `executable` until a measurement says otherwise rather than needing one to get there.

unbound_reason.description: GRAMMAR 1.2. REQUIRED when tier is `unbound` and forbidden otherwise. Must name the engine `ReqKind` that fits this question, and state that the binding and the adversarial pass have not been authored in this standard. Both halves are load-bearing: naming the kind is what distinguishes `unbound` from `blocked` (a `blocked` entry has no kind to name, which is why it cites a G-NN gap instead), and saying the adversarial pass has not happened is what stops the tier being read as `executable`-in-waiting. Where no existing kind fits — a price is published on every product page, but `price_under` needs a cap and there is no `price_is_stated` kind — say that, and file the proposal in ENGINE_GAPS.md rather than writing a binding here.

consumer_note.description: Why this matters to a buyer and how they could check it manually. The half of the document a shopper reads.

merchant_remediation.description: Where truthful evidence should be exposed, in the merchant's own store. Must be a placement instruction, never an instruction to state something that may not be true.

blocked_by.description: ENGINE_GAPS.md identifiers. Required and non-empty when tier=blocked.

known_gaps.description: Pinned adversarial-corpus defects whose shape this entry collides with. An entry that collides with a pinned gap is knowingly unreliable and says so in the published document.

pass_means.description: What a conformant result licenses a reader to conclude, and what it does not. Required for tier=executable. This is the field that stops 'verified against ALS-COFFEE-1.0-CERT-ORG-001' being read as 'certified organic'.

supersedes.description: The entry id in the PREVIOUS version that this entry continues. The id carries the version, so a new version renames every entry; without this field a reader cannot tell a renamed question from a new one, and the old citation's continuity is unverifiable.

allOf.description: THE `unbound` TIER, GRAMMAR 1.2. A binding is forbidden — an entry that has one is either `executable` or is claiming to run something it does not. A `measured_discrimination` is forbidden too, and that is the harder half: a fail rate can only have been produced by RUNNING the entry, so a measurement on an unbound entry is a record of a run the document says never happened. `unbound_reason` is required, so the state is named rather than merely occupied.
And the reason belongs to the tier: `unbound_reason` on any other tier is a sentence about work that is not outstanding.

A claim that a band was measured requires the measurement. `measured: true` on its own is the flattering-instrument failure in miniature: it reads as a verified band and carries no n, no date and no sample. At grammar 1.0 `measured` is const false, so this rule can only ever fire on a hand-edited document — which is precisely when it needs to.

change_type.description: `weakened` = the same store copy that failed before now passes. `demoted` = executable -> advisory/blocked, which has the same effect on a merchant who failed it. `strengthened` = copy that passed before now fails, which is always safe to ship.

weakening_attestation.description: REQUIRED for change_type weakened or demoted. See the never-weaken rule in SCHEMA.md.

vocabularyCitation.description: Grounding for a TERM. Deliberately a separate definition from `#/$defs/grounding`'s citation, because the question is different: an entry's grounding asks whether a SHOPPER asks this question, while a term's grounding asks whether a STORE writes this string. A term invented because it sounds like something a store would write is how a vocabulary becomes plausible and wrong.

kind.description: `process_licensor` and `search_result_snippet` exist only here. A licensor's own page is the authority on how it permits its mark to be written and is NOT independent evidence that the process was used. A search-result snippet is how store copy is observed without fetching a store.

supportingTerm.description: One string whose presence, on an accepted surface, in a sentence that clears the engine's aboutness gates, is accepted as the claim being stated.

term.description: Must already be in engine-normalised form: lower case, single spaces, no leading or trailing whitespace, ASCII hyphens. Enforced behaviourally by standards/vocabulary.ts rule V6, which runs the engine's own `normalize` over it — a term that normalises to something else can never match and would be a silent no-op.

orthography.description: Why this term exists alongside another. `symbol_variant` is the (R)/(TM) case: the engine's `normalize` does NOT strip trademark symbols, so `swiss water process` cannot match `Swiss Water(R) Process` — and a registered mark is exactly what a licensed seller writes. See VOCABULARY_MECHANISM.md section 3.

positive_examples.description: Sentences a store might really write that MUST produce a pass. Executed by the validator: a term whose own examples do not pass is a term that does not work. This is also what forces symbol variants to be enumerated, because an example written with a registered-mark symbol fails until a term matches it.

violatingTerm.description: One string whose presence means the page states the CONTRARY. Checked BEFORE support and winning outright (src/server/productTest.ts:1105), so a wrong violating term does not merely lose a pass — it prints `Your public copy states the opposite of this requirement` beside the merchant's own compliant sentence.

contradicting_examples.description: Sentences that MUST be reported as contradicting. Executed by the validator.

must_not_contradict_examples.description:
THE VIOLATION ATTACK, MADE A REQUIRED FIELD. Sentences in which a COMPLIANT store mentions this substance or method — the free-from constructions, the denials, the scoped negatives — and which must therefore NOT be reported as contradicting. Executed by rule V13.

This field exists because of a measured defect. A bare violating term `methylene chloride` flags the store that writes `Methylene chloride free decaf.`: the term matches, no supporting term overlaps it, and `free` is not in the engine's closed negator list. The fix is to FRAME the violating term — `decaffeinated with methylene chloride` rather than the bare substance — which is the same lesson the engine already learned for attributes, where `materials` uses composition frames because the bare noun `aluminum` would have matched `aluminum-free`. The lesson was never carried across to claims.

Authored rather than auto-generated, so a vocabulary is not failed by a construction no seller would ever write — the precedent being the origin-attribute removal, where a narrowing justified by invented copy cost 17 true statements per 0 false passes gained.

insufficientProbe.description: THE NEGATIVE TEST SUITE, AND THE POINT OF THE FORMAT. Built first, executed by the validator: every example must fail to produce a pass. A vocabulary whose insufficient set does not fail against its own terms is INVALID, not merely under-documented.

example.description: A whole sentence a real store might write. Not a fragment: the engine matches sentence-scoped, so a fragment tests nothing the engine would ever see.

hazard_class.description: The near-miss classes from SCHEMA.md section 2, plus `adjacent_vocabulary` — a DIFFERENT domain vocabulary that legitimately uses the same words. Coffee forced that one: `Process: Washed` names the post-harvest treatment and a decaffeination check keyed on `process` reads a drying method as a solvent disclosure.

expected_outcome.description: The EXACT outcome the validator requires, defaulting to `not_proven`. Asserting an exact outcome rather than merely `does not pass` is deliberate and was forced by a measured defect: a probe can be reported as CONTRADICTING, which prints `Your public copy states the opposite of this requirement` beside the merchant's own sentence — strictly worse for a compliant store than a missed pass, and invisible to a rule that only checks for a pass. `contradicted` is the correct expectation for a negation-class probe where the page really does state the contrary. `passes_known_gap` means the honest answer is that it must not pass and the engine cannot yet refuse it, so the validator requires it to PASS and fails if it ever stops — the adversarial corpus's `actual` vs `correct` mechanism (test/adversarialCorpus.test.ts) ported to vocabularies. A probe pinned that way is a debt with a receipt, never an accepted behaviour.

gap_note.description: Required when expected_outcome is `passes_known_gap`: what makes it uncloseable, and what would close it.

change_type.description: THE NEVER-WEAKEN RULE, EXTENDED TO TERMS. Three of these weaken: `supporting_term_added` (copy that failed now passes), `violating_term_removed` (copy reported as contradicting no longer is), `insufficient_probe_removed` (a form the standard refused is no longer refused). Each requires a weakening_attestation. Their opposites — removing a supporting term, adding a violating term, adding an insufficient probe — are STRENGTHENING and always safe to ship.

detail.description: The term or probe form affected.

vocabulary.description: A VOCABULARY: the term list behind one claim key, published WITH a versioned standard and reviewed AS a standard. The alternative considered and rejected was a `claimVocabulary` override in RunOptions, which would let a term list reach a merchant without any of the review below. See VOCABULARY.md.

claim_key.description: The engine claim key this vocabulary defines. MUST NOT collide with a built-in CLAIM_TERMS key — a registry that can shadow a reviewed built-in list is the (a)-option hazard reintroduced through the back door. Checked by standards/vocabulary.ts.

scope.description: The pass_means of a vocabulary. A term list can establish that a page CLAIMED something; it can never establish that the claim is true. A trademark register resolves ownership of a mark and says nothing about licensees, so even a perfectly matched process name is a claim of fact, not a fact.

serves.description: The standard entries this vocabulary is built for, and HONESTLY how far it takes each one. `narrows` is the common and important case: a claim key answers `is a term present`, so an entry whose operator is equals_one_of is not fully unblocked by a vocabulary alone.

effect.description: `unblocks` = the entry as written becomes executable. `narrows` = a WEAKER sibling assertion becomes executable and the entry as written stays blocked. `supports_refusal_only` = the vocabulary enforces the entry's insufficient set by exclusion without making its positive assertion executable.

accepted_surfaces.description: The surfaces on which a match should be accepted. DECLARED, NOT ENFORCED: the engine's claim branch matches on all six public surfaces including product_title and product_options, both merchant-controlled, and offers no way to restrict them. Measured in VOCABULARY_MECHANISM.md section 6. The gap is filed as part of G-06 rather than papered over.

whole_word.description: NOT a default with an opt-out. The engine hardcodes `{ wholeWord: true }` at the claim call site, so a vocabulary requesting anything else would be describing behaviour the engine cannot produce. The task brief specified a justification field for turning this off; there is nothing to turn off.

violating_terms.description: MAY be empty, and empty is often correct: for most `is a method stated` questions there is no sentence that states the contrary, and absence is not a contradiction. An empty list requires `violating_terms_empty_rationale`, so emptiness is a decision on the record rather than an omission — the same discipline as registry.resolvable being a finding.

limits.description: The false-fail and false-pass channels this vocabulary knows it has and cannot close from the standard side. Honest residual risk beats a claim of immunity.

review.description: The review gate from VOCABULARY_REVIEW.md, recorded in the artifact. `state` is a completion state, not a boolean: `incomplete` BLOCKS publication rather than reading as clean, per src/measure/completion.ts.

adversarial_findings.description: What the attack on THIS vocabulary found. An empty array is permitted only with state `incomplete` — a vocabulary whose attacker found nothing had an attacker who was not trying.

weakeningAttestation.description: THE ONE GOVERNANCE RULE HONOURED FOREVER. The changelog may never show an assertion being weakened in the same window a merchant failed it: that single event retroactively poisons every result the standard ever produced. If failures exist under the prior form, the weakening cannot ship as a silent revision — the affected results must be reissued or invalidated.

prior_failures_exist.description: Were any conformance results issued under the prior form that recorded a failure of this entry?

remediation.description: `not_applicable_no_failures` is ONLY valid when prior_failures_exist is false. Enforced by standards/__tests__ because JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field dependency cleanly.
